description: This topic explores how light bends when it passes between different media, the refractive index, total internal reflection, and how convex and concave lenses form images.

options.text: The bouncing of light off a shiny surface
The bending of light as it passes from one medium to another
The splitting of white light into colours
The complete blocking of light by an object

mcq.explanation: Refraction is the change in direction (bending) of light as it travels from one transparent medium into another of different optical density.

mcq.questionText: Refraction of light is mainly caused by a change in which property of light as it crosses a boundary?
mcq.explanation: Light changes speed when it enters a medium of different optical density, and this change in speed causes the ray to bend.

mcq.questionText: When a ray of light passes from air into glass, it bends towards the normal because glass is:

options.text: The same optical density as air

mcq.explanation: Light travels slower in the optically denser glass, so it bends towards the normal as it enters.

mcq.questionText: When light passes from water into air along the normal (perpendicular to the surface), what happens?

options.text: It bends away from the normal
It passes straight through without bending

mcq.explanation: A ray travelling along the normal hits the surface at 90 degrees, so it does not bend even though its speed changes.

mcq.questionText: The refractive index of a medium is defined as the ratio of:

options.text: The speed of light in the medium to the speed of light in a vacuum
The speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in the medium
The angle of reflection to the angle of incidence
The frequency of light to its wavelength

mcq.explanation: Refractive index n = speed of light in vacuum (or air) divided by speed of light in the medium.

mcq.questionText: The first law of refraction states that the incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in:
mcq.explanation: The first law of refraction states all three lie in the same plane at the point of incidence.

mcq.questionText: The law that states the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant is known as:
mcq.explanation: Snell's law (the second law of refraction) states that sin i / sin r is a constant for a given pair of media.

mcq.questionText: Total internal reflection can ONLY occur when light travels from:

options.text: A less dense medium to a denser medium
A denser medium to a less dense medium

mcq.explanation: Total internal reflection requires light to move from an optically denser to a less dense medium and the angle of incidence to exceed the critical angle.

mcq.questionText: The critical angle is the angle of incidence in the denser medium for which the angle of refraction is:
mcq.explanation: At the critical angle, the refracted ray travels along the surface, making the angle of refraction equal to 90 degrees.

mcq.questionText: A lens that is thicker in the middle than at its edges is called a:
mcq.explanation: A convex (converging) lens is thicker at its centre and brings parallel rays to a focus.

mcq.questionText: A concave lens is also correctly described as a:
mcq.explanation: A concave lens spreads parallel rays apart, so it is called a diverging lens.

mcq.questionText: When parallel rays of light pass through a convex lens, they meet at a point called the:
mcq.explanation: Rays parallel to the principal axis converge at the principal focus (focal point) of a convex lens.

mcq.questionText: Which type of image is always formed by a concave (diverging) lens for a real object?

options.text: Real, upright and the same size

mcq.explanation: A concave lens always produces a virtual, upright and smaller (diminished) image, no matter where the object is placed.

mcq.questionText: Which device uses a convex lens to correct the eye defect known as long-sightedness (hypermetropia)?
mcq.explanation: Long-sightedness is corrected using convex (converging) lenses, while short-sightedness uses concave lenses.

mcq.questionText: A simple magnifying glass produces an enlarged upright image when the object is placed:

options.text: Between the lens and its principal focus

mcq.explanation: When the object is inside the focal length of a convex lens, the image is virtual, upright and magnified, as in a magnifying glass.

fib.questionText: The bending of light as it travels from one transparent medium to another is called _____.
fib.explanation: Refraction occurs because light changes speed when entering a new medium.

fib.questionText: The imaginary line drawn perpendicular to the surface at the point where light strikes is called the _____.
fib.explanation: Angles of incidence and refraction are always measured from the normal.

fib.questionText: When light moves from a less dense to a denser medium, it bends _____ the normal.
fib.explanation: Light slows down in the denser medium, causing it to bend towards the normal.

fib.questionText: The constant ratio sin i / sin r for a given pair of media is known as the _____ of the second medium.
fib.explanation: This relationship is expressed by Snell's law.

fib.questionText: The law stating that sin i / sin r is constant is named after the scientist _____.
fib.explanation: Snell's law is the second law of refraction.

fib.questionText: The smallest angle of incidence in a denser medium for which total internal reflection just begins is called the _____ angle.
fib.explanation: At the critical angle the refracted ray grazes the surface at 90 degrees.

fib.questionText: Optical fibres carry light signals over long distances using the principle of total internal _____.
fib.explanation: Light bounces repeatedly inside the fibre by total internal reflection without escaping.

fib.questionText: A convex lens is also called a _____ lens because it brings parallel rays together.
fib.explanation: Convex lenses cause rays to converge to the principal focus.

fib.questionText: The distance from the optical centre of a lens to its principal focus is called the _____ length.
fib.explanation: A shorter focal length means the lens is more powerful at bending light.

fib.questionText: An image that cannot be formed on a screen because the rays only appear to come from it is described as a _____ image.
fib.explanation: Virtual images, such as those from a magnifying glass, are seen by the eye but cannot be projected.

tf.questionText: Refraction occurs because light changes speed when it passes from one medium to another.
tf.explanation: The change in speed at the boundary causes the light ray to bend.

tf.questionText: A ray of light that strikes a surface along the normal is bent away from the normal.
tf.explanation: A ray travelling along the normal passes straight through without bending.

tf.questionText: When light passes from glass into air, it bends away from the normal.
tf.explanation: Moving into the less dense medium, light speeds up and bends away from the normal.

tf.questionText: The refractive index of a vacuum is exactly 1.
tf.explanation: Since refractive index compares the speed of light in vacuum to itself, it equals 1.

tf.questionText: Total internal reflection can occur when light travels from air into water.
tf.explanation: Total internal reflection only happens when light goes from a denser to a less dense medium.

tf.questionText: At the critical angle, the angle of refraction is 90 degrees.
tf.explanation: The refracted ray travels along the boundary at exactly the critical angle.

tf.questionText: A concave lens is thicker at its centre than at its edges.
tf.explanation: A concave lens is thinner in the middle; it is the convex lens that is thicker in the middle.

tf.questionText: A convex lens can form both real and virtual images depending on the object's position.
tf.explanation: Beyond the focus it forms real images; within the focal length it forms a virtual magnified image.

tf.questionText: A concave lens always forms a virtual, upright and diminished image of a real object.
tf.explanation: No matter where the object is, a diverging lens forms a smaller upright virtual image.

tf.questionText: Convex lenses are used in cameras to focus light and form an image on the film or sensor.
tf.explanation: The camera lens is a converging lens that produces a real, inverted, diminished image on the sensor.

summary.correctAnswer: The bending of light as it passes between media of different optical density.
summary.explanation: It happens because light changes speed at the boundary.

summary.correctAnswer: A change in the speed of light when entering a new medium.
summary.explanation: Slower light bends towards the normal; faster light bends away.

summary.correctAnswer: The ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to its speed in the medium.
summary.explanation: A higher refractive index means the medium is optically denser.

summary.correctAnswer: The incident ray, refracted ray and normal all lie in the same plane.
summary.explanation: This is one of the two laws of refraction.

summary.correctAnswer: The ratio sin i / sin r is constant for two given media.
summary.explanation: This constant equals the refractive index.

summary.correctAnswer: Light is completely reflected inside a denser medium when the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.
summary.explanation: It requires travel from a denser to a less dense medium.

summary.correctAnswer: The angle of incidence in the denser medium that gives an angle of refraction of 90 degrees.
summary.explanation: Above this angle, total internal reflection occurs.

summary.correctAnswer: A converging lens, thicker in the middle, that brings parallel rays to a focus.
summary.explanation: Used in magnifying glasses, cameras and to correct long-sight.

summary.correctAnswer: A diverging lens, thinner in the middle, that spreads parallel rays apart.
summary.explanation: It always forms a virtual, upright, diminished image.

summary.correctAnswer: Lenses are used in cameras, spectacles, microscopes, telescopes and magnifying glasses.
summary.explanation: The type and focal length chosen depend on the required image.

hoq.questionText: A ray of light travels from air into a glass block at an angle of incidence of 60 degrees. If the refractive index of the glass is about 1.5, what can be said about the angle of refraction?
hoq.explanation: Light entering the denser glass bends towards the normal, so the angle of refraction is smaller than the angle of incidence.

hoq.questionText: A medium has a critical angle of 42 degrees with air. If light inside this medium strikes the surface at an angle of incidence of 50 degrees, what happens?

options.text: The light refracts and passes out into the air
The light undergoes total internal reflection
The light travels along the surface at 90 degrees
The light is absorbed by the medium

hoq.explanation: Since 50 degrees is greater than the critical angle of 42 degrees, the light is totally internally reflected back into the medium.

hoq.questionText: An object is placed at a distance equal to twice the focal length (2F) in front of a convex lens. Which best describes the image formed?

options.text: Real, inverted and the same size as the object

hoq.explanation: When an object is at 2F of a convex lens, the image forms at 2F on the other side and is real, inverted and the same size as the object.
